problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨2t,\,{t}^{3},\,{t}^{2}⟩.$ Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,3{t}^{2},\,2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,6t,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨2,\,3{t}^{2},\,2t⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,6t,\,2⟩ \\  & =18{t}^{3}+4t \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(3{t}^{2})^{2}+(2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+9{t}^{4}+4{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{18{t}^{3}+4t}{\sqrt{4+9{t}^{4}+4{t}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
